title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-740. Military Occupational Specialty 740A-Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear
(CBRN) Warrant Officer
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. DA Circular 601 series.
    c. MOS 740A. MOS 740A is an accession MOS. The primary enlisted MOS feeders are 74D (CBRN
Specialist).
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8–-Instructor.
         (3) P–-Parachutist.
         (4) T–-Transition (personnel only).
    e. Associated ASI.
         (1) L3 – Advanced CBRNE Enabler
         (2) L6--Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Reconnaissance
         (3) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Successfully complete the CBRN Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
               (b) Have 20/20 correctable vision and normal color discrimination per AR 40-501.
               (c) Have normal hearing.
               (d) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Successfully complete the CBRN Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualification described in paragraph f(3).
               (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Serves as the standards and certification technician in a narrow technical functional area,
in a CBRN Company and a CBRN Response Team in a Technical Escort Company.
               (b) Manage, instruct and supervise personnel in the technical aspects of CBRN operations.
               (c) Manage the company/team Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) certification program.
       (d) Estimate requirements for personnel, equipment, user/organizational maintenance and repair of
CBRN systems.
               (e) Review, consolidate and prepare technical reports associated with CBRN operations in
assigned unit.
               (f) Assist in coordination and implementation of CBRN operations, and training programs.
               (g) Develop standard operating procedures and performs administrative duties related to
CBRN operations.
         (2) CW3--
               (a) Perform duties described in paragraph g(1).
               (b) Serves as a CBRN technician in mid-level management positions; generally in CBRN
Battalion and Division CBRN Staffs.
               (c) Serves as the division commander’s senior technical advisor/analyst in all areas of CBRN
operations.
               (d) Provide technical guidance to personnel of supported units/activities in order to establish
and maintain adequate CBRN operation techniques for mission accomplishment.
         (3) CW4--
               (a) Performs duties described paragraphs g(2).
               (b) Serves as the senior CBRN technician in positions requiring advanced level technical
skills; generally at CBRN BN, CBRN BDE, and Corps CBRN staffs
               (c) Responsible for coordinating CBRN operation activities with all subordinate units and
integrating CBRN operations with higher echelon organizations.
              (d) Provides direct interface with elements involved in joint, interagency, intergovernmental,
multinational (JIIM), and combined arms CBRN operations.
              (e) Serves in positions requiring advanced technical skills to perform duties related to CBRN
training and evaluation and the development of standard operating policy and doctrine.
              (f) Instructs and provides technical advice in the management and maintenance of CBRN
operation systems.
        (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties as described in paragraphs g(3).
              (b) Serves as the most senior CBRN technician in positions that require unusual depth and
breadth of technical knowledge for functional training and curriculum development or major systems
integration skills.
              (c) Provides technical advice and assistance in regards to CBRN operations in CBRN BDEs,
to include all aspects of training, personnel, doctrine, force structure, requirements and use/maintenance
of CBRN operations systems.
              (d) Develop, review and updates the life-cycle management of the CBRN technician’s
structure and force.
              (e) Perform duties as proponent level personnel systems integrator.
              (f) Instructs and monitors students in a service school environment.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
           (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
           (2) Qualifying Scores.
              A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) –
0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 Shuttles in Physical
Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
           (3) Table 8-740A-1. Physical requirements.
           (4) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3: W4 equals CW4; W5 equal CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
               (a) Table 8-740A-2. Standard of grade TOE/MTOE.
               (b) Table 8-740A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
